Direction answer (folded in as required): PROCEED. This is the shortest safe path to the next result and does not grow overhead: it is a minimal, correct equivalence/accounting connection that unblocks the already-reviewed normal admission without any new science, money, or provenance package. The past-failure pattern (infrastructure proving infrastructure) is not repeated here because the change adds one tiny 39-line encoder-alignment module plus two bounded reuse wrappers of existing proofs, with no new subsystem.

Independent judgment: The behavioral core is a genuine, minimal bug fix. The retained-terminal proof pins are produced with modal_executor.canonical (spaced JSON) in tools/item4_validation_retained.py, but the original consumer compared with review_submission.canonical (compact separators), so byte-identical rows were rejected (ITEM4_VALIDATION_TERMINAL_ROW_CHANGED, reproduced in ADMISSION_CLONE_READONLY.stderr and in the producer_encoded_terminal test). The new item4_terminal_row_encoding.retained_terminal is a line-for-line copy of the original verifier changing only the local row encoder to modal_executor.canonical, so consumer and producer encodings now match while every gate, identity, set and per-row comparison is preserved. This is an equivalent-or-stronger replacement, not a weakening, consistent with the operator's delegation that a blocking check may be replaced by an equivalent one but never removed.

The two bundled connections are tightly bound and non-mutating. connect_spending imports the byte-exact original protected module at its reviewed path, runs its own implementation() verifier, and pins source/review. connect_original_call reuses the existing R42 author5 native-terminal proof at the spending boundary only for the exact active run, exact ledger scope, a read-only local SQLite handle, and a single hardcoded call id (49cc364b..., the one UNCERTAIN author5 call not yet qualified per PENDING_CALL_DIAGNOSIS); it adds only that id to the returned closed set, leaving the UNCERTAIN row and its full charge intact and releasing nothing, which satisfies the operator rule against releasing reservations for open/uncertain attempts. All stale/foreign/unknown/live/changed records keep their ordinary refusals, verified by the 9-way refusal parametrization run against the fixed module.

Caps, confinement and scientific status are untouched: SMOKE/PROJECTION/TOTAL caps remain 75M/1200M/1275M micro-USD; the memory-only clone admits a normal reservation at 10342400 micro (inside $75) and the independent over-cap clone refuses with ITEM4_HARD_COST_CAP, with zero real reservations/compute and originals hashed unchanged; scientific REVISE10 preserves U1/U2/U3 as open findings. Tests genuinely reproduce the mismatch and then prove preserved charges, over-cap refusal, and every rejection path (181 pass); the only two failures are an unrelated absent-live-fixture case that reproduces identically on the parent and is disclosed. No secret values appear in the changed files and confinement settings in the (unchanged) providers are intact.

The change sits squarely in the engineering/accounting act-freely lane, crosses no operator hard line (no new spend, no patient access, no credentials, no confinement weakening, no merge/history/ledger rewrite, no BACKLOG change), and I found no test-set/leakage, code/spec mismatch, metric, privacy/secret, budget, or execution-authority/provenance defect.
